items.title: Cisco patches actively exploited Secure Email Gateway zero-day
items.summary: Cisco released fixes for CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS 9.8), an arbitrary file write flaw in Secure Email Gateway's Advanced Malware Protection that lets an unauthenticated attacker send a crafted attachment and execute commands with root privileges. Cisco says active exploitation began in October 2026; there is no workaround and the flaw has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

items.title: California student data breach exposes millions of records
items.summary: The California Department of Education confirmed hackers used a compromised credential to access Educational Testing Service systems from May 22 to September 18, 2026, copying records of all California public school students enrolled over the past three years plus some former students dating back to 2006. Exposed data includes names, addresses, birth dates, student IDs and assessment data; Social Security numbers and financial data were not accessed.

items.title: Burger King Japan data breach exposes 11 million customer records
items.summary: Burger King Japan disclosed that attackers accessed a server holding 11.18 million customer records — names, dates of birth, genders, email addresses, phone numbers and order history of official app users — between October 2 and October 7, 2026, with data leaked online. The company says no credit card numbers were stored on the server and no user credentials were accessed.

items.title: Hackers use compromised ConnectWise credential to sign in to 173 Microsoft 365 tenants
items.summary: Huntress found attackers abusing a compromised ConnectWise credential to access 173 Microsoft 365 tenants, inheriting the backup application's broad permissions over mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams and directory data — some of it readable with no audit trail. Researchers advise disabling the app until ConnectWise confirms a credential reset, enabling Graph activity logs, and auditing for new credentials added since October 13.

items.title: Rhysida ransomware gang lists 2.6TB of Maryland county data for sale
items.summary: Anne Arundel County, Maryland confirmed an unauthorized actor copied files from a limited number of government systems during an August 28 cyberattack. The Rhysida gang claims it stole 814,500 files (2.6TB) — including medical faxes, Social Security numbers, payroll and jail records — and is advertising the data on its leak site for 25 BTC (about $2 million).

items.title: GitLab patches max-severity vulnerability CVE-2026-97229
items.summary: GitLab released emergency fixes for CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 10.0), an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular expression compiler that could let an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code on the server via a crafted regex in a CI/CD configuration. It affects GitLab CE/EE 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2; no exploitation has been observed yet.
